turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, Dr. [Name], I—I suppose I should just start by explaining how things are set up at the office, because otherwise none of this is going to make any sense to you. I'm the CEO, so my office shares a wall with the main executive conference room. And lately, I... I came in today because I keep hearing them talking about me. The board members, mostly, and some of my senior staff. 

I'll just be sitting there, trying to review our quarterly projections, and I can hear them right through the walls, just whispering and talking, saying that I’m completely ruining the company. That I'm driving it into the ground. And the thing is, it’s not even just the walls. It’s my phone, too. I’ll actually power the device completely down—screen black, sitting right there on my desk—and I can still hear their voices coming out of the speaker. 

It’s so... it’s so incredibly clear. I mean, the acoustics of it, the exact tone of their voices, it sounds so real that I actually answer them. I’ll say, out loud, "If you have a problem with my leadership, come in here and say it to my face!" and I'll be halfway through defending my executive decisions before I realize... before I realize that my assistant is staring at me from the doorway and no one else actually heard a single word. But I hear it. I hear them all the time. And I just—I don't know how I'm supposed to run a corporation when this keeps happening, so I had to come see someone.

symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient describes hearing voices of board members and staff criticizing him through walls and a powered-off phone, which are clear auditory hallucinations occurring without an external stimulus.
